subject: On-prem logchain & SIEM audit plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <security@blackboxsec.com>, ops@acme.example
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem logchain & SIEM audit plan

Jordan / ACME team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our call, we want to lock down a lightweight, auditable plan for shipping logs/traces from the on-prem enclave to your SIEM (BlackBox) for the POC. High-level asks below; please confirm constraints and anything we missed.

Summary goals:
- End-to-end auditability: origin marker on each event + delivery acknowledgements
- Minimize egress surface: single, authenticated outbound channel preferred
- Retention and lineage: logs retained in-customer for 90 days; exported copies retained by BlackBox per contract

Questions / decisions needed:
1) Preferred transport: syslog TCP/TLS, HTTP HEC (token/mTLS), or SFTP drop? Which fits your ingestion best?
2) Certificate requirements for mTLS (client certs from customer vs. Redwood-managed)?
3) Delivery ACK semantics: do you require guaranteed-at-least-once replay vs. near-real-time best-effort?
4) Trace sampling: what level of trace sampling do you need for distributed tracing hooks (full traces for errors, sampling for normal traffic)?

Attachments: log-retention-spec-v1.pdf (draft), trace-hook-checklist.csv

Suggested next steps: Ben can provision a constrained forwarder container for the enclave and we can run an internal dry-run with a test HEC endpoint. If that looks good we schedule an egress test window (2hrs) with your ops team.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[attachment: log-retention-spec-v1.pdf (pdf)] [attachment: trace-hook-checklist.csv (csv)]

From: Jordan Lee <security@blackboxsec.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme.example
Date: Tue, 18 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem logchain & SIEM audit plan

Mina —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from BlackBox side:

- Preferred transport: HEC over HTTPS with token auth or mTLS. If you can do mTLS that's ideal; token-only is acceptable for the POC but we'll prefer mTLS for production.
- Certificates: we can accept customer-supplied client certs signed by a public CA, or we can provide a CA bundle for you to sign against. If you manage the client certs inside the enclave that minimizes our operational load.
- Delivery ACK: we need at-least-once semantics for security logs (auth, suspicious activity) for audit windows. For lower-priority app logs, best-effort is fine.
- Trace sampling: full traces for error/alerting paths; 1% sampling for standard request traces. We can tune later.

We have a small constraint: we cannot accept inbound SFTP drops for structured events (parsing/latency reasons). Also we cannot accept unauthenticated syslog. HEC or syslog over TLS with mutual auth are the only viable choices.

I'll loop in our ops contact if we need to lock down an IP allowlist for the POC.

Jordan Lee
Director, Security Integrations
BlackBox Security

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <security@blackboxsec.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem logchain & SIEM audit plan

Thanks — quick technical proposal from infra: we can run a hardened forwarder inside the customer enclave (container + sidecar) with the following pattern:

Design summary:
- Single egress tunnel: HTTPS to a validated HEC endpoint on port 8088. Tunnel uses mTLS (client cert) issued by customer PKI for production; for POC we can use short-lived client certs Redwood issues and rotate.
- Envelope metadata: forwarder will add a redwood.origin_id and an internal sequence id to every event; those are included in the HEC payload so BlackBox can ack/record them.
- ACK model: forwarder queues events to local durable spool (fsync) then POSTs to HEC. On 2xx/3xx we mark delivered. On 4xx/5xx we back off and retry with exponential backoff; we keep offsets for at-least-once replay on failure.
- Network egress: only the forwarder gets egress permission, and we restrict outbound to the BlackBox HEC FQDN(s). We will publish an egress CIDR list in advance for allowlist.
- Trace hooks: we'll propagate traceparent and baggage fields. For error buckets we include full-span export. For sampled traces we respect sampling rate (1% default).

Proof artifacts attached: forwarder-config.example (yaml), network-egress-diagram.png

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- If customer requires zero external cert management, we can run HEC token auth but will need signed attestations and shorter token TTLs.
- For high-volume telemetry (embeddings / token-level logs) recommend local aggregation + batched POSTs. Real-time security streams (auth failures) will be forwarded immediately with higher priority.

Next steps: Mina — if you confirm mTLS + at-least-once for security logs, I’ll prepare the forwarder image and a 2-hour egress test plan. Laura / Tessa — please confirm retention instrumenting on the customer side (we need the 90-day local retention configured and a snapshot/manifest exported to BlackBox during onboarding).

Ben Carter
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem logchain & SIEM audit plan — next steps and schedule

Thanks all — good alignment. Finalizing plan and next actions below so we have a single source of truth.

Decisions:
- Transport: HEC over HTTPS with mTLS for production; POC may use short-lived client certs Redwood rotates.
- ACK model: at-least-once for security logs, best-effort for lower-priority metrics/logs.
- Retention: customer to retain 90 days locally; BlackBox will persist according to contract.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Ben: build forwarder image and config (forwarder-config.example), provide a staging HEC URL and egress CIDRs. ETA: 2028-07-24 EOD.
- Jordan / BlackBox: provide preferred CA bundle or onboarding token and confirm HEC ingestion thresholds. ETA: 2028-07-22.
- Laura / Tessa: verify customer-side retention snapshot and manifest process; supply runbook for audit extraction. ETA: 2028-07-23.
- Mina: schedule POC egress window (2hrs) and runbook review; will send calendar invite. ETA: 2028-07-21.

I’ll attach the final retention spec and a compact runbook to the Confluence page and post the HubSpot deal update when Ben confirms the staging endpoint.

Thanks —
Mina
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
